h: FG targets 40% cut in transport fares with new CNG buses
p: The Presidency says it is targeting a 40% reduction in commercial transport fares through a programme to bring hundreds of CNG-powered buses onto Nigerian roads, starting with 100 buses.
body: President Bola Tinubu's administration says it is targeting a 40% reduction in commercial transport fares through a new programme to bring hundreds of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses onto Nigerian roads.

The plan was announced on Thursday, 19 November 2026, in a statement by the President's Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. It is anchored on a new agreement with a bus manufacturer, and the statement gave details of when the first 100 buses are expected to arrive.

The government has been promoting CNG as a cheaper alternative to petrol and diesel. It recently announced plans for 167 new CNG refuelling stations and highlighted a CNG price of ₦430.

Chinese manufacturer Yutong has agreed to set up a CNG bus assembly plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, under a deal with the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles. It will initially supply 300 CNG buses, with the first 100 expected in Lagos before the end of December 2026.

The government has also begun installing CNG refuelling stations and conversion centres in 20 federal universities under a scheme called Project SPROUT, to cut campus transport costs. Education Minister Tunji Alausa announced the start of the rollout while commissioning the facilities at the University of Lagos.
